If you're forecasting your digital media spend, you need to compare the ROI of your display ads, paid social, Google Ads, and social media. Depending on your objectives, it's worth reviewing and benchmarking the latest metrics like average click-through rates, average cost per click, and cost per lead.

I've put this compilation together to help marketing professionals create direct response conversion models for digital marketing campaigns. ### Average CTR benchmarks - February 2024 update

We’ve updated our compilation of average clickthrough rates, cost per click, and cost per lead across Google Ads, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and LinkedIn.

Each year, we update our statistics summaries with the latest research as it becomes available. Stats are in three sections which answer these questions:

- Q. What are average display ad CTRs for different industries?
- Q. What average CPC/ cost per lead can industry marketers expect?
- Q. What are social media ad clickthrough rates - a comparison of Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and Twitter CTRs?

### Search Marketing Benchmarks: Average click-through rate

One of the best sources for PPC data is [LocalIQ/Wordstream paid search benchmarks](https://www.wordstream.com/online-advertising-benchmarks). Note that the sample is typically for smaller local businesses.  The data below details their most recent CTR, CPC, CR and CPL in 2023 for a wide range of business categories:

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Google-Ad-response.png)

Of course, these figures are averages for each sector across CTRs which tend to be higher for brand searches and lower for generic searches.

**Note on data source:**

This chart is based on a sample of c5,000 North American-based LOCALiQ client accounts in the home services vertical who were running search advertising, display advertising, and/or social media advertising . Each subcategory includes a minimum 10 unique active clients. “Averages” are technically median figures to account for outliers.

#### CPC cost per click/ cost per lead search advertising benchmarks

However, it's important to look at the bigger picture when defining the value of your clicks. $9 is still a very reasonable cost considering the high-value potential for each customer lifecycle in this industry. Therefore it's reasonable to presume that the CPC is driven up by high competition for a relatively smaller number of target customers (/clicks).

We also have a comparison of [Google organic Clickthrough rates by position](https://www.smartinsights.com/search-engine-optimisation-seo/seo-analytics/comparison-of-google-clickthrough-rates-by-position/).

#### Alternative data on CTRs for larger businesses

For brand engagement rates, one of the best sources for insight on paid media engagement including CTR and cost is the [Skai research](https://skai.io/reports-and-whitepapers/). Skai (formerly Kenshoo) is a performance marketing platform offering advertising Placements on Google, Meta, Amazon Ads, TikTok, Snap, Walmart Connect, Instacart, Roundel, Criteo, CitrusAd, Pinterest, Microsoft, Apple Search Ads, and more.

Brands using it include Pepsico, Diageo, Reckitt, Daimler, LG, and Vodafone. It is one of the few sources available offering CTR benchmarks for search and display. Trends in retail categories are also shown in the full report. The most recent version published as of Jan 2024 includes Q3 of 2023, these are shared below.

**Paid search (Google Ads) CTR and CPC trends for retail**

These Clickthrough rates give a basic benchmark, but include both brand and product-based searches.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/2025-04-09_09-48-33-1.png)

#### **Paid social CTR**

Unfortunately, there isn't a breakdown by social network in the Skai data, but the majority of the spend is with Meta platforms Facebook and Instagram. This shows how CTR is typically around 1.1-1.3% in social feeds which is significantly higher than the lower historic data reported for display towards the end of this article.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/2025-04-09_09-52-28.png)

Further insight on organic and paid social engagement across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok is available from the Emplify (formerly Social Bakers) [social media industry reports](https://emplifi.io/resources/industry-benchmarks) which cover 6 industries.

### Google Ads (formerly AdWords) display network benchmarks

LocalIQs [Google Adwords industry benchmarks average CTRs](https://localiq.com/blog/search-advertising-benchmarks/) now report just on the Google Ads search network accounts they manage. They no longer report on the display network. This typically has sub one-percent CTRs.

#### Google Doubleclick benchmarks for ad placement

Unfortunately, Google has removed CTRs reported for its Doubleclick display brand and their interactive Display benchmarking tool.  So now we can only present previous data. No other alternatives are available as far as I'm aware.

> _Previous pre-2015 Doubleclick data shows an average CTR of just 0.05% for all display formats, i.e just 5 clicks per 10000 impressions, showing the difficulty of driving direct response from online display or banner ads. Perhaps that is why Google no longer publishes this data..._

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/Display-ad-clickthrough-rates-latest-captured-January-2018-700x400.png)

While this is a really low CTR, however you look at it, cross-media optimization tests shows that online ads do help increase brand awareness and purchase intent, particularly when combined with offline media.

It's not the case that the majority of ad viewers have 'banner blindness' and are not aware of ads that are viewable placements. If this were the case, businesses wouldn't invest in the level of display and programmatic ads that they do.

We also see much higher CTRs online for other online ad formats like Google AdWords and Facebook - these can exceed 1%, so are more effective in driving volume and also typically have higher intent, so conversion rates are higher.

Tests from the likes of Dynamic Logic and Millward Brown conclusively show that display ads also encourage site visits (view throughs) and searches even where people don't click on ads.

**Variation in online average CTRs by ad format**

Ad clickthrough rate naturally varies according to placement (position on screen) and ad format (shape and size). The traditional full-banner performs very poorly compared to skyscrapers, the ubiquitous medium rectangle and the newer large rectangle format.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/12/EMEA-Ad-Clickthrough-rates.png)

### Variation in online ad Interaction Rates by ad format

Interaction rates differ for different ad formats in a similar way to ad formats.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/12/EMEA-Ad-Interaction-rates1.png)

**Interaction rate definition**:

Interactions are defined as the user does one or more of the following:

- Mouses over the ad for 1 continuous second
- Clicks an Exit link
- Makes the ad display in Full Screen mode
- Expands the ad

#### Google responsive display ads

Note that more recently Google introduced [Responsive Display ads](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6363750?hl=en-GB) on the Google Display Network as the default ad type. These involve uploading your assets (images, headlines, logos, videos and descriptions) and Google will automatically generate ads to be shown on the Google Display Network.

Reports from early adopters suggest that these can have relatively high CTRs. This example of [CTRs compared a Google Ads campaign](https://www.theppcmachine.co.uk/responsive-display-ads-versus-image-ads) provided by Smart Insights Expert commentator David Miles. It shows the uplift he received when testing this new format.

### What are social media average CTRs - a comparison of Facebook and Twitter?

Unfortunately there are no recent benchmarks for individual Meta platforms other than those from Skia above. The examples below are dated from a [Q1 2020 ad benchmark report.](https://www.adstage.io/resources/adstage-benchmark-reports/) Here are the median CTRs for their clients in North America:

#### Facebook ad CTR

The average Facebook CTR in the newsfeed is 1.11%. This is trending downwards; a decrease of 0.37% compared to the previous year.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/2020-Facebook-ad-clickthrough-rates-700x531.png)

Other data reported includes:

- CTR on the right side placement averages just 0.16%.
- Facebook Stories have an average CTR of 0.79%.
- [Facebook Audience network](https://www.facebook.com/business/marketing/audience-network) is 0.69% (mainly used for promoting apps such as gaming apps on publisher sites and in apps). This uses a [range of ad formats](https://www.facebook.com/audiencenetwork/solutions/ad-formats) such as display, native and video.

#### Instagram ad CTR

Instagram ad clickthrough rate in the feed is 0.22%, significantly lower than in the previous year and much lower compared to Facebook. This reflects the visual nature of Insta which doesn't offer opportunities for CTR in organic newsfeeds (other than Stories). Benchmarks for Stories are a little higher at 0.33%.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/2020-Instagram-ad-clickthrough-rates-700x526.png)

#### LinkedIn Ad CTR

Although the audience is quite different since LinkedIn targets B2B audiences, there is a similar CTR in LinkedIn of 0.22%.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/2020-LinkedIn-ad-clickthrough-rates-700x608.png)

#### Twitter Ad CTR

Twitter has a higher clickthrough rate, although there is a significant decrease in the last quarter. Fewer impressions are served to Adstage customers in this category so this insight should be treated with caution.

![](https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/2020-Twitter-ad-clickthrough-rates-700x692.png)

                <h2>Our latest summary of ad clickthrough rates statistics in the US, Europe, and Worldwide is designed to help you benchmark your paid digital and social media ads, set marketing budgets, and define your goals</h2>
<p>If you're forecasting your digital media spend, you need to compare the ROI of your display ads, paid social, Google Ads, and social media. Depending on your objectives, it's worth reviewing and benchmarking the latest metrics like average click-through rates, average cost per click, and cost per lead.</p>
<p>I've put this compilation together to help marketing professionals create direct response conversion models for digital marketing campaigns. By creating budget models using known benchmarks for average CTRs and digital media click-through costs, you can better forecast your return on investment from digital media ads. Our budgeting and forecasting spreadsheets include:</p>
<ul>
<li><a class="more-link" href="https://www.smartinsights.com/guides/digital-marketing-planning-spreadsheet/" data-wpel-link="internal">Simple digital channel planning spreadsheet</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.smartinsights.com/guides/conversion-optimisation-calculator/" data-wpel-link="internal">Conversion and revenue model spreadsheet</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.smartinsights.com/guides/online-customer-acquisition-budget-spreadsheet/" data-wpel-link="internal">Month-by-month customer acquisition spreadsheet</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.smartinsights.com/guides/marketing-budget-spreadsheet-template/" data-wpel-link="internal">Monthly marketing budget spreadsheet</a></li>
</ul>
<p>This data is particularly useful if you haven't previously invested in advertising on publisher sites through ad networks or paid social media ads since it can help make the case and set expectations with colleagues or clients of the number of visits based on quantitative forecasts. As always, we recommend applying a targeted, data-driven approach to your marketing activities and we have tools and templates to help.</p>

<h3>Average CTR benchmarks - February 2024 update</h3>
<p>We’ve updated our compilation of average clickthrough rates, cost per click, and cost per lead across Google Ads, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and LinkedIn.</p>
<p>Each year, we update our statistics summaries with the latest research as it becomes available. Stats are in three sections which answer these questions:</p>
<ul>
<li>Q. What are average display ad CTRs for different industries?</li>
<li>Q. What average CPC/ cost per lead can industry marketers expect?</li>
<li>Q. What are social media ad clickthrough rates - a comparison of Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and Twitter CTRs?</li>
</ul>
<h3>Search Marketing Benchmarks: Average click-through rate</h3>
<p>One of the best sources for PPC data is <a href="https://www.wordstream.com/online-advertising-benchmarks" data-wpel-link="external" rel="nofollow external noopener noreferrer">LocalIQ/Wordstream paid search benchmarks</a>. Note that the sample is typically for smaller local businesses.  The data below details their most recent CTR, CPC, CR and CPL in 2023 for a wide range of business categories:</p>
<p><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-169769 size-full" src="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Google-Ad-response.png" alt="" width="1098" height="925"></p>
<p>Of course, these figures are averages for each sector across CTRs which tend to be higher for brand searches and lower for generic searches.</p>
<p><strong>Note on data source:</strong></p>
<p>This chart is based on a sample of c5,000 North American-based LOCALiQ client accounts in the home services vertical who were running search advertising, display advertising, and/or social media advertising . Each subcategory includes a minimum 10 unique active clients. “Averages” are technically median figures to account for outliers.</p>
<h4>CPC cost per click/ cost per lead search advertising benchmarks</h4>
<p>However, it's important to look at the bigger picture when defining the value of your clicks. $9 is still a very reasonable cost considering the high-value potential for each customer lifecycle in this industry. Therefore it's reasonable to presume that the CPC is driven up by high competition for a relatively smaller number of target customers (/clicks).</p>
<p>We also have a comparison of <a href="https://www.smartinsights.com/search-engine-optimisation-seo/seo-analytics/comparison-of-google-clickthrough-rates-by-position/" data-wpel-link="internal">Google organic Clickthrough rates by position</a>.</p>
<h4>Alternative data on CTRs for larger businesses</h4>
<p>For brand engagement rates, one of the best sources for insight on paid media engagement including CTR and cost is the <a href="https://skai.io/reports-and-whitepapers/" data-wpel-link="external" rel="nofollow external noopener noreferrer">Skai research</a>. Skai (formerly Kenshoo) is a performance marketing platform offering advertising Placements on Google, Meta, Amazon Ads, TikTok, Snap, Walmart Connect, Instacart, Roundel, Criteo, CitrusAd, Pinterest, Microsoft, Apple Search Ads, and more.</p>
<p>Brands using it include Pepsico, Diageo, Reckitt, Daimler, LG, and Vodafone. It is one of the few sources available offering CTR benchmarks for search and display. Trends in retail categories are also shown in the full report. The most recent version published as of Jan 2024 includes Q3 of 2023, these are shared below.</p>
<p><strong>Paid search (Google Ads) CTR and CPC trends for retail</strong></p>
<p>These Clickthrough rates give a basic benchmark, but include both brand and product-based searches.</p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-169763" src="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/2025-04-09_09-48-33-1.png" alt="" width="1466" height="592"></p>
<h4><strong>Paid social CTR</strong></h4>
<p>Unfortunately, there isn't a breakdown by social network in the Skai data, but the majority of the spend is with Meta platforms Facebook and Instagram. This shows how CTR is typically around 1.1-1.3% in social feeds which is significantly higher than the lower historic data reported for display towards the end of this article.</p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-169764" src="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/2025-04-09_09-52-28.png" alt="" width="1502" height="612"></p>
<p>Further insight on organic and paid social engagement across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok is available from the Emplify (formerly Social Bakers) <a href="https://emplifi.io/resources/industry-benchmarks" data-wpel-link="external" rel="nofollow external noopener noreferrer">social media industry reports</a> which cover 6 industries.</p>
<h3>Google Ads (formerly AdWords) display network benchmarks</h3>
<p>LocalIQs <a href="https://localiq.com/blog/search-advertising-benchmarks/" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow external noreferrer" data-wpel-link="external">Google Adwords industry benchmarks average CTRs</a> now report just on the Google Ads search network accounts they manage. They no longer report on the display network. This typically has sub one-percent CTRs.</p>
<h4>Google Doubleclick benchmarks for ad placement</h4>
<p>Unfortunately, Google has removed CTRs reported for its Doubleclick display brand and their interactive Display benchmarking tool.  So now we can only present previous data. No other alternatives are available as far as I'm aware.</p>
<blockquote><p><em>Previous pre-2015 Doubleclick data shows an average CTR of just 0.05% for all display formats, i.e just 5 clicks per 10000 impressions, showing the difficulty of driving direct response from online display or banner ads. Perhaps that is why Google no longer publishes this data...</em></p></blockquote>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-108472 size-large" src="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/Display-ad-clickthrough-rates-latest-captured-January-2018-700x400.png" alt="" width="640" height="366"></p>
<p>While this is a really low CTR, however you look at it, cross-media optimization tests shows that online ads do help increase brand awareness and purchase intent, particularly when combined with offline media.</p>
<p>It's not the case that the majority of ad viewers have 'banner blindness' and are not aware of ads that are viewable placements. If this were the case, businesses wouldn't invest in the level of display and programmatic ads that they do.</p>
<p>We also see much higher CTRs online for other online ad formats like Google AdWords and Facebook - these can exceed 1%, so are more effective in driving volume and also typically have higher intent, so conversion rates are higher.</p>
<p>Tests from the likes of Dynamic Logic and Millward Brown conclusively show that display ads also encourage site visits (view throughs) and searches even where people don't click on ads.</p>

<p style="text-align: left;"><strong>Variation in online average CTRs by ad format</strong></p>
<p>Ad clickthrough rate naturally varies according to placement (position on screen) and ad format (shape and size). The traditional full-banner performs very poorly compared to skyscrapers, the ubiquitous medium rectangle and the newer large rectangle format.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/12/EMEA-Ad-Clickthrough-rates.png" data-wpel-link="internal"><img decoding="async" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-3795" title="EMEA-Ad-Clickthrough-rates" src="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/12/EMEA-Ad-Clickthrough-rates.png" alt="" width="584" height="334"></a></p>
<h3>Variation in online ad Interaction Rates by ad format</h3>
<p>Interaction rates differ for different ad formats in a similar way to ad formats.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/12/EMEA-Ad-Interaction-rates1.png" data-wpel-link="internal"><img decoding="async" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-3797" title="EMEA-Ad-Interaction-rates" src="https://www.smartinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/12/EMEA-Ad-Interaction-rates1.png" alt="" width="609" height="307"></a></p>
<p><strong>Interaction rate definition</strong>:</p>
<p>Interactions are defined as the user does one or more of the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>Mouses over the ad for 1 continuous second</li>
<li>Clicks an Exit link</li>
<li>Makes the ad display in Full Screen mode</li>
<li>Expands the ad</li>
</ul>

<p>Reports from early adopters suggest that these can have relatively high CTRs.
